title: Atomic rollback cookbook and comm ladder (Apr 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact cookbook for performing minimal-impact (atomic) rollbacks during staged rollouts, and a communication ladder to avoid noisy all-hands notifications for every minor revert. It's intended for release engineers, on-call SREs, and the duty release lead.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) deployments.
- Covers four atomic rollback classes: feature-flag flips, model-variant swaps, small infra patch rollbacks (pool/node), and config/migration toggles.

Definitions:
- Atomic patch: a single, reversible action with a predictable short window of impact (<= 30m to revert).
- Release lead: person managing the rollout window.
- Duty SRE: primary on-call for infra and traffic management.

Pre-rollback checklist (5-minute sanity):
- Confirm observable signal: graph spike, error class, or regression from evaluation prompt set.
- Check canary slice telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by route).
- Confirm latest deploys: git commit, image tag, model version. (git log & runtime API)
- Notify release lead + duty SRE on Slack #release-ops (short message).
- If customer-facing error, page immediately following standard incident triage.

Atomic rollback recipes (concise, tested steps):
1) Feature flag toggle (fastest)
- When to use: bug introduced by new code path guarded by flag or unsafe experiment.
- Steps:
  1. Open feature-flag service console (flags.redwood.internal).
  2. Flip flag from ON -> ROLLBACK (or OFF for simple flags).
  3. Run quick smoke: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer smoke-token" \"https://staging-api.redwood.ai/health?route=canary\" and check response.
  4. Observe telemetry for 2 minutes; if stable, announce in-thread and resume rollout.
- Expected timeframe: 30–90s to flip, 2–10 minutes to validate.
- Rollback notes: leave flag in ROLLBACK until follow-up PR or hotfix.

2) Model variant swap (model serving change)
- When to use: regressions in generation quality or massive latency increase after model swap.
- Steps:
  1. Identify current model alias and previous stable alias (e.g., model-chat-v2 -> model-chat-v1-stable).
  2. Use admin API to set alias: POST /admin/model/alias {"alias":"chat-default","model":"model-chat-v1-stable"} 
     Example: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" -d '{"alias":"chat-default","model":"model-chat-v1-stable"}' https://admin-api.redwood.local/admin/model/alias
  3. Purge prefix cache for canary routes: POST /cache/prefix/clear {"prefix":"/canary/"}
  4. Run sample eval prompts (10 representative prompts) via qa harness.
  5. Validate latencies and quality metrics (rollout dashboard).
- Expected timeframe: 2–5 minutes for alias flip, 10–20 minutes for full metric convergence.
- Rollback notes: if alias flip exposes cache or KV issues, fall back to traffic split (see traffic-split recipe).

3) GPU pool drain -> fallback lane (infrastructure-level)
- When to use: node-level regressions, hardware kernel mismatch, or OOM spikes.
- Steps:
  1. Move canary traffic off pool: update routing policy to exclude pool-id (route-rule API). Example: PATCH /routing/policies/canary {"exclude_pools":["pool-east-3"]}
  2. Trigger graceful drain via infra API: POST /pools/{pool-id}/drain?mode=graceful
  3. If drain cannot complete within N minutes, trigger emergency shift to fallback pool with warm instances.
  4. Monitor queued requests and throttling.
- Expected timeframe: 5–20 minutes depending on inflight requests.
- Rollback notes: do not delete pool until drain completes and metrics return to baseline.

4) Config/migration toggle (DB flags, feature-gates)
- When to use: config-backed regressions or failed backward-incompatible change.
- Steps:
  1. Revert config change in config store (ksctl or config service).
  2. If schema migration caused error, run the compatible down-migration or run application-level compatibility shim: set env VAR MIGRATION_SAFE=true.
  3. Validate reads/writes on a sampled tenant.
- Expected timeframe: depends on migration size; aim for atomic toggles under 30m.

Smoke-test checklist (post-rollback verification):
- Verify p95 latency back within 10% of baseline for the impacted routes.
- Error rate reduced to baseline within 5 minutes.
- No new high-rate exceptions in logs for 15 minutes.
- Run 20 quick QA prompts through the harness and confirm no semantic regressions.

Communication ladder (who to message and how):
- Step 0 (immediate): release lead posts short alert in #release-ops with one-line summary and action (e.g., "rollback: feature flag X flipped, monitoring"), mention duty SRE.
- Step 1 (if >15m active work or customer-visible): post update in #incident and tag product engineering manager + CS lead.
- Step 2 (if >60m or high-sev customer impact): page on-call and escalate to Eng Director.
- Templates (short):
  - Slack: "[ROLLBACK] short-desc | action taken: {flip/alias/pool-drain} | ETA validate: 10m | lead: @aisha"
  - Pager (if paging): include runbook link and minimal steps executed.

One-week rollout calendar (compact):
- Mon 09:00–12:00: Canary ramp for release X (owner: Marcus) — small traffic slice -> smoke tests -> roll to 25% if green.
- Tue 14:00–16:00: Observability audit and staged model swap (owner: Sofia) — run eval suite post swap.
- Wed 11:00–13:00: Flag-based feature flips for opt-in customers (owner: Aisha) — monitor CS tickets.
- Thu 17:00–18:30: Night window: limited rollout to 50% with throttles (owner: Tom) — standby SRE.
- Fri 10:00–11:00: Canary validation and release notes cut (owner: Aisha)
Notes: Keep windows short, communicate to CS before customer-facing changes.

Release notes (draft to paste in GH release/confluence):
Title: Rolling release X — Apr 2027 (canary -> gradual)
Summary: Small staged rollout to improve chat-quality and reduce hallucination on long prompts. This rollout introduces a model variant and two small feature flags.
What changed:
- Model: model-chat-v2 (improved coherence for long context).
- Flags: streaming-improve-buffer (opt-in), reranker-bias-fix (opt-out by default).
Rollout plan:
- Day 0: Canary at 5% in us-west for 2 hours; smoke tests and evals.
- Day 1–3: Incremental ramp to 50% with telemetry gates.
Known issues:
- Observed p95 latency bump on some edge routes when prefix caching is cold.
- Small increase in token usage for a subset of prompts.
Rollback plan summary:
- Feature issues: flip flag to OFF (recipe 1).
- Model issues: alias back to model-chat-v1-stable (recipe 2).
- Infra issues: drain pool and shift traffic (recipe 3).
Post-deploy triggers for postmortem:
- >5% sustained error-rate delta for 30 minutes, or customer SLA violations affecting >1% of customers.

Quick checklist for the release lead (one-line):
- Confirm artifacts (image/model/flags) - confirm hashes.
- Run preflight smoke & eval.
- Open release channel + set notifications.
- Start canary -> observe -> execute rollback recipe if signals fail.
- If rollback, run smoke-test checklist and close channel with short postmortem note.

Notes & follow-ups (open actions):
- Marcus: add a lightweight metric to signal model-quality (open ticket RELEASE-3490).
- Sofia: validate cache-purge scripts for alias flips (PR in runtime repo).
- Aisha: draft customer-facing blurb if rollback becomes user-visible.

Appendix — quick command snippets (replace tokens/hostnames):
- Alias flip: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin' -d '{"alias":"chat-default","model":"model-chat-v1-stable"}' https://admin-api.redwood.local/admin/model/alias
- Cache purge: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin' -d '{"prefix":"/canary/"}' https://admin-api.redwood.local/cache/prefix/clear
- Flag toggle: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ff-admin' -d '{"flag":"streaming-improve-buffer","state":"off"}' https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggle

End of draft. Keep this near-horizon and iterate after the next postmortem so recipes are fully automated where possible.
